summary: DB-023 created public.event_posts in the active chain (20260928010000_event_posts_and_event_claims.sql) and established the disclosure decision that previously existed nowhere in the schema. Four call-site defects surfaced while doing so are in the events lane's files and are NOT fixed here, because app/api/events/** is outside DB-023's grant. (1) PGRST EMBED. app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts:42 and app/api/events/[id]/page/route.ts:121 both select `profiles:user_id (...)`. PostgREST can only satisfy that with a foreign key to public.profiles, and the migration keeps the canonical shape (`user_id uuid references auth.users(id)`), the same shape as public.posts (20240430000000:6). The repository has already paid for this exact bug: lib/feed/feed-posts-query.ts:3 records 'Intentionally no `profiles:user_id (...)` embed: many environments lack a posts->profiles FK (PGRST200)' and hydrates owner profiles in application code instead. So once the table exists, these two routes move from 'relation does not exist' to 'could not find a relationship between event_posts and profiles'. That is a narrower, named failure with a precedent to copy. Do NOT add an event_posts->profiles foreign key to silence it; that would invent an authorization-relevant constraint and make these two routes the only place in the repository relying on such an embed. (2) CLIENT-SIDE WRITE. components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx:221 inserts straight to PostgREST through the anon/authenticated browser client, with only a client-side `canPost` flag in front of it (line 199). The installed policy event_posts_own_insert is `auth.uid() = user_id AND (visibility = 'public' OR EXISTS(attending))`, so ANY signed-in account can post a public post on ANY event id, with no organizer, attendee or event-existence check. That is the recorded authorization model from the archive, not a widening made by the migration, and narrowing it in SQL would break the documented behaviour of app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts. The fix belongs here: route the component's write through the API route, or accept the spam surface explicitly. (3) UNVALIDATED VISIBILITY. app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts:90 takes `visibility` from the request body with no validation, and the installed CHECK admits exactly ('public','attendees'), so a caller-supplied 'organizers' is refused with 23514 and the route returns 500. A zod enum is the fix. Note the CHECK was derived from the literals live code writes or reads (components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx:103 types the union; lib/feed/attending-event-posts.ts:220 filters on them), so this is not the schema narrowing a value the product wants. (4) A GRANT TWO ROUTES ALREADY NEEDED AND NEVER HAD. app/api/events/[id]/posts/route.ts:113 and app/api/events/[id]/page/route.ts:97 read public.event_attendance through the CALLER's client, and 20250814091000 creates that table with no grant and the chain has no `alter default privileges`. The attendance check therefore fails silently today (posts/route.ts ignores the error, so `isAttending` stays false; page/route.ts logs it). The migration issues `grant select on public.event_attendance to authenticated` and asserts it, so this is fixed by the apply -- but the routes' SILENT handling of that error is a defect of its own, and it is what hid the missing grant until now. One disclosure question is OPEN and is the events lane's to answer, not the database lane's: the installed read policy is `visibility = 'public' OR auth.uid() = user_id` (unscoped) plus an `attendees` arm scoped to authenticated. There is NO predicate on the parent event's publication state, because event_table discriminates three parent relations and this migration does not own the event publication contract. Consequence, measured: anon holds SELECT, so a public-visibility post of a DRAFT or CANCELLED event is readable by anyone holding the anon key who knows the event id. Deciding whether that is acceptable, and closing it if not, needs the publication predicate for public.events, public.artist_events and public.events_v2 together.

completed: DB-023 side: the table, the four policies, the grants and the contract are authored and proved (154/154 on a throwaway cluster). Nothing in app/ was edited.

COMPLETION CONDITION MET, ALL FIVE PARTS. (1) The `profiles:user_id` embed is removed from both routes and owners are hydrated in application code, following lib/feed/feed-posts-query.ts:3, via one shared derivation in app/api/events/_lib/event-post-owners.ts. The rejected alternative -- adding a foreign key to public.profiles -- is recorded in the module's doc comment, in EVENTS-005's AC-1, and enforced by a test that asserts the migration's event_posts block still contains `user_id uuid not null references auth.users(id)` and no `references public.profiles`. (2) The client-side insert is ROUTED THROUGH THE API: components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx now POSTs to /api/events/[id]/posts and no longer inserts into event_posts directly. The permissive authorization model recorded in this handoff is UNCHANGED and was deliberately not accepted in writing; what changed is that the permissive policy is now the only write path, so it is narrowable later in one place. (3) `visibility` AND `type` are validated with zod enums via safeParse, so an unadmitted value is a 400 with the offending field named and NO write attempted -- not a cast, and not a 23514 reported as a 500. All four admitted type literals are accepted and asserted to write the validated value. (4) The event_attendance read error is handled EXPLICITLY in both routes. posts/route.ts additionally moved .single() to .maybeSingle() (a zero-row match was PGRST116 through the catch block into a 500) and fails closed on the elevated arm only: an unreadable attendance row blocks an `attendees`-visibility post and still permits a `public` one, which is the arm the installed policy permits for any signed-in account anyway. page/route.ts states the failure in the response contract (`attendance.unavailable`, `posts_unavailable`) and forces can_post false, instead of returning a page indistinguishable from one nobody engaged with. (5) THE PUBLICATION-STATE QUESTION IS ANSWERED, NEGATIVE, AND THE RESIDUAL IS ROUTED -- see HF-EVENTS-005-EVENT-POSTS-ANON-READ-RESIDUAL. No policy can close it for the `anon` role: a publication predicate must branch on three parent relations, and 20260928010000's own header records the measured consequence, that a policy OR containing a subplan over a table the evaluating role cannot read fails the WHOLE query with 42501 rather than failing the disjunct. `anon` holds no SELECT on public.events, public.artist_events or public.events_v2, so a publication predicate would make every anonymous read of an event post fail -- a launch outage, and the exact failure the migration avoided by splitting its attendees arm into a role-scoped policy. The installed policy is therefore the correct schema-side posture. THE RESIDUAL IS REACHABLE AND IS NOT CLOSED: components/events/enhanced-event-page.tsx:120 reads event_posts through the browser client, whose key is the anon key, filtered only on (event_id, event_table = 'events') with no publication check, reached from app/events/[slug]/page.tsx with no auth gate. So a public-visibility post on a DRAFT legacy events row is readable by anyone holding the anon key who knows the event id. EVENTS-005 did not move that read, because AC-2 names the write and the read change alters loading behaviour on a public launch surface with no stated criterion; it is routed to a bounded successor instead of absorbed. BOTH API READERS KEEP `canAccessEventAsViewer` and are pinned by tests that a now-existing RLS policy is not a reason to delete them.
